- Mitigation: open a soft burst window from the shared pool for 45 minutes while we triage (need ops authorization).
- Business: surface impact and recommend credit path (Rishi, can you advise on credits/contract relief?).

Vanessa / team —

Quick update after immediate checks:
- Root cause (short): a combination of an unexpected burst from a batch of long-context inference jobs plus a recent slot fragmentation after an autoscaler shift. The reserved pool's headroom dropped below the token-threshold for safe batching, which caused long tails and eventual 5xx backpressure in the queue manager.
- Evidence: token-queue length trended from 12 -> 78 in 8 minutes; GPU utilization spiked to 98% on the affected shard. I attached a snippet of the scheduler trace to the incident page (internal link in related_links).

Short-term mitigations I can enact now (15-30m impact window):
1) Route non-critical endpoints to our hosted-optimized variant (lower-cost model, same API surface) — will reduce load on reserved pool by ~30%.
2) Temporarily enable KV prefix caching for session-heavy chat flows — expected p95 reduction ~35%.
3) Throttle background/analytics inference across your reservation (configurable token quota per minute).
4) If authorized, open a soft shared-pool burst (45m) to absorb the current backlog while we rebalance.

I recommend doing 1+2 immediately. I'm standing by to flip the routing and caching flags; we need operations sign-off for the shared-pool burst (Marissa).

-David
